[Source 1] Code Generation with LLMs: Codex, CodeLlama, and Programming Assistants
Code Llama, released by Meta AI in August 2023, presents a family of code-specialized language models based on Llama 2. Code Llama is fine-tuned on 500B tokens of code-heavy data with a long-context fine-tuning (LCFT) phase that extends the context window from 4K to 100K tokens via position interpolation. The model family includes base models (7B, 13B, 34B), instruction-following variants (Code Llama Instruct), and Python-specialized variants (Code Llama Python). The 34B model achieves 53.7% pass@1 on HumanEval and 56.2% on MBPP. Codex (Chen et al., OpenAI, 2021) established the benchmark by fine-tuning GPT-3 on 159GB of Python code from GitHub, achieving 28.8% pass@1 on HumanEval. GPT-4 later achieved 67.0% pass@1 on HumanEval.

Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) training is a key capability in Code Llama. By rearranging 50% of training examples as prefix-suffix-middle, the model learns bidirectional code infilling—given surrounding code context, generate the missing middle section. This enables intelligent code completion (as opposed to left-to-right generation), the primary use case in IDE integrations. Code Llama achieves 74.0% on the MultiLine Infilling benchmark. Long context handling (up to 100K tokens) enables repository-level code understanding: retrieving relevant function definitions, class hierarchies, and usage patterns from large codebases before generating new code. DeepSeek-Coder (Guo et al., 2024), trained on 2T tokens from 87 programming languages with 16K context, achieves 79.3% pass@1 on HumanEval for the 33B model, surpassing GPT-4.

Production code generation systems such as GitHub Copilot report that 46% of code in supported languages is now written by AI (GitHub, 2023), with developers reporting 55% faster task completion. StarCoder (Li et al., 2023, BigCode) provides a 15.5B code model trained on The Stack (6.4TB of permissively licensed code from 358 programming languages), achieving 40.8% on HumanEval with commercial licensing. By eliminating the memory bottleneck, FlashAttention enables training on significantly longer sequences, instrumental in extending context windows for models like Llama 2 (4K), Code Llama (100K), and Mistral (32K with sliding window attention). FlashAttention-3 targets H100 hardware, achieving 740+ TFLOPs/s for FP16.

[Source 3] Quantization for LLMs: GPTQ, QLoRA, and INT8 Inference Techniques
d mixed CPU/GPU inference, enabling quantized LLaMA models to run on Apple Silicon, consumer gaming GPUs, and CPUs. Supported quantization types include Q4_K_M (4-bit with mixed 6-bit precision for critical layers), providing the best quality-size trade-off. llama.cpp achieves 30-50 tokens/second on Apple M2 Pro for Llama 3 8B in Q4_K_M quantization. AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization, Lin et al., 2023) identifies salient weight channels corresponding to large-magnitude activations and applies higher precision only to those channels, achieving 4-bit quality closer to FP16 than GPTQ. LLM.int8() (Dettmers et al., 2022) handles outlier activations via mixed-precision decomposition, enabling 8-bit inference with negligible quality loss for models up to 175B parameters.
